lessons.title: Language: Double Comparatives
objectives: Nắm vững các khái niệm và định nghĩa cốt lõi của Language: Double Comparatives.
Hiểu và áp dụng thành thạo các quy tắc và công thức trong SGK 12.
Rèn luyện kỹ năng phân tích và giải quyết các bài toán/tình huống thực tiễn ôn thi THPT & ĐGNL.

concepts.definition: Structure expressing proportional relationship where a change in one factor directly causes a corresponding change in another factor.
concepts.example: The more modern a city becomes, the higher the cost of living gets. The more trees we plant, the cleaner the air will be.
concepts.essence: Expressing continuous parallel progression and cause-effect correlation dynamically.

concepts.definition: An urban area that uses Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, data analytics, and digital technology to manage assets, resources, and services efficiently.
concepts.example: Smart traffic lights automatically adjust timing based on real-time vehicle density to minimize gridlock.
concepts.essence: Technological integration transforming urban governance and sustainability.

rules.statement: Word order in double comparative structures
rules.meaning: Both clauses start with 'The' followed by comparative adjective/adverb/noun, then subject + verb: The + comparative + S + V, the + comparative + S + V.
rules.example: The more carefully you plan, the better results you will achieve.
rules.essence: Symmetrical structural balance between dependent and independent clauses.

workedExamples.prompt: Rewrite using double comparative: 'As cities grow bigger, traffic congestion becomes worse.'
steps: Step 1: Identify the two changing elements: cities grow bigger -> The bigger cities grow;
Step 2: Traffic congestion becomes worse -> the worse traffic congestion becomes.
Step 3: Combine with parallel symmetry: The bigger cities grow, the worse traffic congestion becomes.
workedExamples.answer: The bigger cities grow, the worse traffic congestion becomes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Omitting 'the' before one of the comparatives: *More you practice, the better you become*.
commonMistakes.why: Both parts must strictly start with 'The': The more you practice, the better you become.
